_note: Skeleton for docs/law-uuid-exemptions.json — the factory data file read by tests/test_law_no_raw_session_uuid.py. Copy it into docs/ (the example itself is never read) and add an entry ONLY where a raw 36-character session uuid in a LAW file is genuinely NOT a routing instruction a reader follows. The gate's population is every law file — skills/*/SKILL.md, SKILL.md.tmpl and TEMPLATE/SKILL.md.tmpl — and the measured defect it was built for is real: skills/meta-factory/SKILL.md's substrate-routing table named `d72bd52d-42aa-4dbd-ac99-5b5300770019` for OpenCrabs HQ, and that id carried ZERO bindings, so a reader who followed it reached nobody while the row read exactly like the live id beside it. Section 11's rule is that a lane is addressed by the session id resolved LIVE at dispatch, so a law file carries the topic/role NAME, never the uuid. Key every entry by `path` + `uuid` — IDENTITY, never a line number, which rots on the first insertion above it. Every entry that MATCHES prints as an `excused:` line on EVERY run, so it is visible debt rather than forgiveness, and the closing line distinguishes clean from excused. An entry that matches NOTHING is a gate ERROR rather than a silent pass, so a retired debt cannot sit in the file looking live; a malformed or duplicated entry is an ERROR too. Absent or empty means NO EXEMPTIONS, never a failure — a bootstrapped factory starts clean, which is why this skeleton ships `exempt: []` and this repo's own five entries stay in docs/ and never travel. State `reason` (why this occurrence is not a routing instruction) and `proof` (the read that establishes it); an entry a reader could not defend in the gate's own output is one to fix instead of excusing. What this table CANNOT do is check freshness: nothing offline can read live session_bindings, so no exemption and no gate can assert that a NAME still resolves. That check belongs to the dispatch-time resolution, and it is stated here rather than faked.
